_note: SYNTHETIC. The sentences the engine really emits, produced by running the real analyzers — never hand-written or sanitized. Regenerate with `python3 scripts/gen_annotation_fixtures.py`.

basal.capped (lower): a step down, limited to 20% below the set rate
basal.capped (raise): a step up, limited to 20% above the set rate
basal.held (recurring-low gate): a low printed at this hour, so a step up is withheld and the rate stays as it is
basal.insufficient evidence: not enough nights of steady data yet to point one way
basal.lower: one cautious step down is supported at this time
basal.lower (recurring lows): lows keep happening at this hour, so the rate steps down toward the measured rate (20% at most)
basal.no baseline: no set rate to step from, so only the measured range is shown
basal.no change: the measured rate and the set rate agree, so no change is suggested
basal.no data: no nights of steady data at this time yet
basal.raise: one cautious step up is supported at this time

isf.collecting_range_too_wide: not enough independent fasting nights yet to suggest a change, so overnight data is still collecting
isf.confirmed: your fasting data agrees with the set correction factor
isf.held_after_a_low: a low after a correction is on record, so the correction factor stays as it is rather than going stronger
isf.held_rescue_log_incomplete: rescue-carb history does not cover part of this window, so a quiet stretch cannot be confirmed and the correction factor stays as it is
isf.no_baseline_measured: measured overnight sensitivity (no set value to compare with)
isf.no_baseline_no_data: not enough steady fasting data yet to measure your correction factor
isf.no_measurement: not enough steady fasting data yet to measure your correction factor
isf.strengthen: overnight you look more sensitive to insulin than the set value, so corrections can run a little stronger
isf.watching_not_yet_held: the overnight reading differs from the set value but has not held across two weekly check-ins, so nothing is suggested yet
isf.weaken_easing: corrections keep overshooting into lows, so the correction factor eases weaker
isf.weaken_easing_disagreeing_measurement: corrections keep overshooting into lows, so the correction factor eases weaker (the overnight reading points the other way, but it is unsteady and the lows carry the decision)
isf.weaken_no_target: corrections keep overshooting into lows, so more overnight data is needed before a new number
